known_blockers: Eight Encyclopedia of Mathematics source locators remain unverified (access errors).

Arithmetic on Cauchy quotient classes and their ordered-field laws still require theorem-level well-definedness and completeness proofs; definition screening does not claim those proofs completed.
The union-of-cuts supremum result and complete ordered-field uniqueness are theorem statements, not new mathematical definitions, and remain excluded from meaning counts.

The coverage validator was generalized to allow more than one independently sourced observation per term; variant-specific source locator checks must use the specific formulation, not the first sibling form.

The 0-inclusive natural-number convention still has an explicitly justified no-supported-target decision pending independently sourced Peano axioms/finite-ordinal characterization; do not create reverse links to integers.

The broad Batch 66–68 σ-algebra and compactness source/variant/link reviews completed. A σ-algebra variant has an explicit no-supported-target disposition rather than invalid recursion; compact and quasicompact are equivalent under non-Hausdorff general topology convention but may differ by Hausdorff requirements in some texts.
Connectedness is CONVENTIONAL rather than an error: Stacks explicitly excludes the empty space, ProofWiki does not. Both source-backed contextual meanings are now preserved under one displayed term.

Continuity source locator resolved in Batch 74; the original guessed Definition:Continuous_Map URL remains invalid, and all screened continuity variants use checked Definition:Continuous_Mapping_(Topology).

All 3 martingale formulation no-supported-target reviews have now been explicitly amended by independently sourced adaptedness and conditional expectation definitions. The primitive stochastic-process formulation now has a justified no-supported-target decision until probability space and general measurable-space/r.v. foundations are separately screened.
Continuous-index adapted process is independently sourced, but only discrete-time filtration has a checked direct source in the corpus; do not link it to real-index adaptedness as if equivalent.
Chromatic polynomial equivalence is still research-only; MathWorld is not in vetted source registry. A new source registration, rights review and exact citation are required before ingesting it.
Metric/nonempty ProofWiki convention was preserved in Batch98; no empty metric-space convention admitted without an additional independent source.

The generic scalar division-ring normed-vector foundation was source- and meaning-screened in Batches100–102 with correct multiplicative and left/right scope; original standalone ProofWiki Normed Division Ring page lists no bibliographic citations. A separate external authority should corroborate when feasible.
Current scalar normed vector source is left-oriented; no right-normed-vector formulation should be automatically generated without specifically sourced right-action homogeneity axioms.

ProofWiki calls its selected-point global-domain bound 'Lipschitz at a point', which is NOT equivalent to neighborhood-local two-point Lipschitz continuity; preserve this distinction in later variant comparisons.
The two tree formulations, no circuits/no cycles, are equivalent only in the stated simple connected undirected graph context; no root or finite-cardinality convention inferred.
Independent sigma-algebra countable-family property imposes all finite distinct-index products; pairwise independence alone does not imply mutual independence for three or more.

ProofWiki Definition:Boundary (Topology) 'Definition from Closure and Exterior' appears false as written: it takes subset of A and omits closure boundary points outside A. Excluded from Batch106/107/108; separate source-audit should note this.

The general closure source also has closure=A union boundary; it was not ingested because allowing boundary to depend on closure and closure to depend on boundary would form a definition expansion cycle. Source-preserved noncircular closed-superset formulations were admitted instead.
ProofWiki source-specific finite-image rank requires the image of a field-vector-space linear transformation to be finite-dimensional; no automatic cardinal-valued or arbitrary-module rank extension.
Accumulation point of a sequence (infinitely many indices in each neighborhood) differs from accumulation point of its value SET (closure of A minus the tested point); do not collapse variants.

Source audit Batch112: ProofWiki Definition:Directional Derivative says gradient-dot-unit-vector under merely 'gradient exists', mathematically insufficient if gradient denotes existing coordinate partials; counterexample xy/(x²+y²), f(0,0)=0. Source observation .02 deliberately quarantined, not approved mathematical form. Total differentiability is sufficient for equivalent line restriction formula.

Closed metric ball at radius r can strictly contain closure of corresponding open ball in a general metric space (e.g. discrete metric radius 1). Do not infer equality from an overbar notational convention.

The three specifically identified definition dependency target gaps from Batch120 (subgroup, left coset/coset product, real power-series convergence) were source-reviewed and retroactively linked in Batch124; broader undiscovered missing targets may still exist.
Previously source-held ProofWiki Graph Isomorphism one-way-edge clause and Directional Derivative gradient-only clause still excluded from approved mathematical meanings.

Batch125 ProofWiki Uniform Convergence Infinite Series section incorrectly writes partial sum s_n(x)=Σ_{k=1}^n f_n(x) rather than Σ f_k(x); source observation held and excluded from screened meanings.

The exact two B127 logged prerequisite target gaps (product topology on function space T^D, eigenvalue of K-linear operator) were independently sourced in B128–130 and separately backfilled in B131, with no cyclic link or historical decision rewrite.

ProofWiki Definition:Degree of Vertex incident-edge count equals distinct-neighbor count only for simple loopless graphs, not general multigraphs; accepted both forms only under explicit simple-graph scope.

The B134 missing target coverage categories (numeric Kronecker delta, falling factorial at k=0, convex subset of real vector space) were independently source-reviewed in B135–137 and retroactively linked to Stirling and convex-hull formulations in B138; still not exhaustive coverage.

Source-scope caution: ProofWiki Definition:Falling Factorial itself has n>0 only; x falling to zero equals 1 is justified separately by ProofWiki Binomial Coefficient with Zero. Do not misattribute the extension.
